rotation_note: Unattended-run override: NO rotating subset. All 3 core keywords plus the entire politics pool (34 keywords, grouped into policy_regulation / elections_public_opinion / geopolitics) are working keywords today. Day-of-year 308 sets ORDER only: group start index 308 % 3 = 2 (policy_regulation leads, then elections_public_opinion, then geopolitics), and within each group the list starts at offset 308 % group_size in pool order (policy 15 -> 8: NIST AI framework first; elections 9 -> 2: synthetic media election first; geopolitics 10 -> 8: AI 패권 first). Queries were not checked with WebSearch (budget reserved for librarians); librarians should prefer outlet RSS/sitemap_news feeds over site: search for recency. Window: last brief was 2026-11-03, so items published 11-03 (after the prior harvest) through 11-04 are in scope. Context: 2026-11-04 is the day after the US midterm Election Day. In scope: official post-election statements on AI-enabled interference (CISA/FBI/ODNI, state election officials), platform takedown/labeling reports covering election day, certified outcomes of AI-specific ballot measures (e.g. data center siting/moratorium, AI-related state propositions), and FEC/FCC actions. OUT of scope: who won, seat counts, polling, horse-race analysis, and candidate-level AI super PAC spending commentary (Bellingcat super PAC story covered 11-03). Lame-duck session agenda items count only when a bill is introduced/marked up or an official release names AI. EU: informal European Council in Dublin on AI 2026-11-13 upcoming (official pre-meeting papers are new; previews are not). Neutrality rule from sources.json applies: report decisions/filings/releases, attribute contested claims, no partisan framing.
